person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A CONSENSUS DEFINITION REVISED WHILE ITS THREE CATEGORY NAMES STAY PUT - `proven`, `probable` and `possible` invasive fungal disease keep their labels from 2008 while `probable` is expanded and `possible` is shrunk, so the same three words now denote different sets of patients
span.quote: There is no change in the classifications of “proven,” “probable,” and “possible” IFD, although the definition of “probable” has been expanded and the scope of the category “possible” has been diminished.

span.label: how to extend research definitions of invasive fungal disease beyond cancer and transplant patients, what to do about tests that did not exist or were unstandardised in 2008, and where the boundary of each category should now sit
span.quote: The 2008 definitions had their shortcomings, including the facts that the definitions were unsuitable for patients with IFD in the setting of intensive care units (ICUs) or in pediatrics, data were insufficient to establish appropriate thresholds for detecting Aspergillus galactomannan (GM), and there was uncertainty about the role of (1,3)-beta-D glucan (BDG). Furthermore, nucleic acid amplification including polymerase chain reaction (PCR)–based tests were excluded because of lack of standardization and validation. Definitions for cryptococcosis and endemic mycoses also needed clarification, and there were no definitions for pneumocystosis.

span.label: revised definitions of proven, probable and possible IFD - new host factors, new radiological features, thresholds for galactomannan that replace the manufacturer's, the admission of Aspergillus PCR, and first definitions for non-HIV pneumocystosis
span.quote: European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer and the Mycoses Study Group definitions for probable invasive fungal disease now include solid organ transplant, hematologic malignancy, graft-versus-host disease, the reverse halo sign, revised thresholds for galactomannan, Aspergillus polymerase chain reaction, and definitions for candidiasis, cryptococcosis, non-human immunodeficiency viirus–associated pneumocystosis, and endemic mycoses.

span.label: method
span.quote: Importantly, these definitions are specifically intended for these purposes only and not to direct or guide patient care.

span.label: a group of diseases that can rarely be proven in life, so that the categories researchers count are degrees of certainty rather than states of the patient
span.quote: Tissue diagnosis requires the presence of fungal elements in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue and signifies proven fungal disease but not the identity of the fungus involved.

span.label: 10 working groups of EORTC and MSGERC volunteers, each appraising one topic, presented at a conference, opened for public comment for three months, and iterated to a manuscript approved by all members
span.term: 10 working groups of EORTC and MSGERC volunteers, each appraising one topic, presented at a conference, opened for public comment for three months, and iterated to a manuscript approved by all members
span.quote: Volunteers from the EORTC Infectious Diseases Group and the MSGERC were assigned according to their expertise to 10 working groups, each charged with appraising a particular topic (see list of contributors in the Notes section). The chairs of the EORTC and MSG (J. P. D. and P. G. P.) selected leaders for each working group, and S. C. served as executive secretary. After completing the first round of working group assignments, leaders presented each group’s initial deliberations and recommendations at the 7th Trends in Medical Mycology Conference in Lisbon, Portugal, October 2015. A slide set was made available until 31 December 2015 online at www.e-materials.com/timm2015/invitation/Member and, on request, for public comment. After several iterations, the final draft of the manuscript was circulated to all members for their approval.

span.label: **THE LABELS DID NOT CHANGE AND THE CLASSES DID**: `There is NO CHANGE IN THE CLASSIFICATIONS of `proven,` `probable,` and `possible` IFD, ALTHOUGH THE DEFINITION OF `PROBABLE` HAS BEEN EXPANDED AND THE SCOPE OF THE CATEGORY `POSSIBLE` HAS BEEN DIMINISHED.` **A trial reporting `probable IFD` in 2010 and one reporting it in 2021 are not counting the same patients, and neither label says so.** The corpus holds definitions that moved and were renamed; this one moved and kept its name, which is the harder case to detect downstream
span.quote: There is no change in the classifications of “proven,” “probable,” and “possible” IFD, although the definition of “probable” has been expanded and the scope of the category “possible” has been diminished.

span.label: **AND THE DEFINITION IS EXPLICITLY NOT FOR TREATING ANYONE**: `Importantly, these definitions are SPECIFICALLY INTENDED FOR THESE PURPOSES ONLY AND NOT TO DIRECT OR GUIDE PATIENT CARE.` Restated at the end: `we have emphasized the need to DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN DEFINITIONS OF IFD REQUIRED FOR CLINICAL RESEARCH FROM THOSE THAT INFLUENCE CLINICAL PRACTICE. In clinical practice, MANY WOULD ADMINISTER AN ANTIFUNGAL AGENT ... WITHOUT THERE BEING SUFFICIENT EVIDENCE TO SATISFY THE CONSENSUS DEFINITIONS OF IFD.` **A definition bounded by PURPOSE, not by population or by evidence base** - and the authors say plainly that practice does not follow it and should not
span.quote: Importantly, these definitions are specifically intended for these purposes only and not to direct or guide patient care.

span.label: **AND FOR ELEVEN YEARS THE THRESHOLD BELONGED TO THE ASSAY MANUFACTURER**: `there was NO AGREEMENT ABOUT APPROPRIATE THRESHOLDS, so THE MANUFACTURERS' ANALYTICAL THRESHOLDS WERE ADOPTED.` This revision takes it back - `REVISED THRESHOLDS FOR GM NOW REPLACE THOSE OF THE MANUFACTURER` - and the replacement still names a brand: `A single threshold (>80 pg/mL) using the FUNGITELL test ... is recommended; there is INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE TO INCLUDE ASSAYS PRODUCED BY OTHER MANUFACTURERS.` **The boundary of a disease category was, and partly still is, a commercial parameter**
span.quote: In the previous definitions [ 1 ], indirect tests for diagnosing IFD were only included if there was sufficient evidence that they had been standardized and validated. Moreover, commercial tests were included only if criteria for interpretation had been provided. Hence, while tests for GM and BDG were incorporated, tests for detecting fungal nucleic acid were not [ 1 ]. Furthermore, there was no agreement about appropriate thresholds, so the manufacturers’ analytical thresholds were adopted.

span.label: AND THE THRESHOLD WAS DELIBERATELY INDEXED TO THE SPECIMEN RATHER THAN THE PATIENT: `We adopted DIFFERENT THRESHOLDS FOR DIFFERENT SPECIMENS RATHER THAN FOR DIFFERENT HOST GROUPS.` Two ways to make one test mean the same thing across a population, and the choice is stated. **Compare prigerson2009, where items that behaved differently across host groups were DELETED rather than re-thresholded**
span.quote: We evaluated Aspergillus galactomannan for both adults and children and specific patient groups and its utility and validity for different clinical specimens. We adopted different thresholds for different specimens rather than for different host groups [ 33–35 ] ( Table 2 ).

span.label: **AND A WORKING GROUP FAILED AND SAID SO**: `group 10 (IFD definitions in ICU patients) WAS UNABLE TO GENERATE RECOMMENDATIONS THAT PRESERVED A LEVEL OF CERTAINTY CONSISTENT WITH THE EXISTING DEFINITIONS except for proven IFD, and therefore undertook a separate initiative.` One of ten groups reports that its population cannot be brought inside the definition at the certainty the definition requires. **The honest outcome of an extension attempt, printed rather than papered over**
span.quote: However, group 10 (IFD definitions in ICU patients) was unable to generate recommendations that preserved a level of certainty consistent with the existing definitions except for proven IFD ( Table 1 ) and therefore undertook a separate initiative [ 8 ].

span.label: **AND A TERM WAS STRUCK OUT FOR IGNORANCE**: `'COLONIZATION' with Cryptococcus spp. IS NO LONGER INCLUDED IN THE DEFINITIONS AS IT IS POORLY UNDERSTOOD and its natural history is unknown.` simonneau2018 KEEPS a whole class - group 5 - for precisely this reason, `the LACK OF ROBUST DATA allowing a definite recognition of predominant pathophysiological mechanisms`. **Same criterion, opposite operation: one field files the not-understood into a class of its own, the other deletes the term**
span.quote: “Colonization” with Cryptococcus spp. is no longer included in the definitions as it is poorly understood and its natural history is unknown.

span.label: AND ANOTHER TERM WAS ABANDONED FOR A PARTITION: `The term `DISSEMINATED CRYPTOCOCCOSIS` as distinct from CNS cryptococcosis HAS BEEN ABANDONED IN FAVOR OF THE TERMS `PULMONARY,` `CNS` AND `OTHER EXTRAPULMONARY SITES.`` A term whose meaning was `everything beyond one site` replaced by naming the sites. **A negative definition traded for an enumeration**
span.quote: The term “disseminated cryptococcosis” as distinct from CNS cryptococcosis has been abandoned in favor of the terms “pulmonary,” “CNS” and “other extrapulmonary sites.”

span.label: AND A CLASS WAS EXTENDED TO PEOPLE WITH NO SYMPTOMS: `we also recognize cryptococcal infection among individuals in high-risk host groups WHO HAVE FEW, IF ANY, SYMPTOMS AND ONLY A POSITIVE SERUM CRYPTOCOCCAL ANTIGEN TEST (asymptomatic cryptococcal antigenemia). THIS CONDITION MAY BE MORE COMMON THAN SYMPTOMATIC DISEASE ... and so are NOW INCLUDED IN THESE DEFINITIONS.` The justification is prognostic - they `MAY DEVELOP CLINICAL CRYPTOCOCCAL DISEASE UNLESS TREATED` - which is simonneau2018's argument for the 21-24 mmHg band, in a different discipline the same year
span.quote: However, we also recognize cryptococcal infection among individuals in high-risk host groups who have few, if any, symptoms and only a positive serum cryptococcal antigen test (asymptomatic cryptococcal antigenemia). This condition may be more common than symptomatic disease, and patients may develop clinical cryptococcal disease unless treated and so are now included in these definitions [ 70 ].

span.label: **AND THE FIELD HAD TO WRITE DOWN THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TWO OF ITS OWN WORDS**: `There is MUCH CONFUSION ABOUT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A HOST FACTOR AND A RISK FACTOR. As before, A HOST FACTOR HAS BEEN DEFINED AS A CHARACTERISTIC OF INDIVIDUALS CLEARLY PREDISPOSED TO, AND NOT SIMPLY AT RISK OF, AN IFD. For example, while IMPAIRED GUT WALL INTEGRITY ... MAY INCREASE THE RISK of candidiasis, IT WAS NOT CONSIDERED SPECIFIC ENOUGH to warrant inclusion as a host factor.` **A worked example of the line between a constituent and a correlate** - and simonneau2018 demotes splenectomy across the same line in the same year
span.quote: While definitions of proven and probable disease have been shown to be reliable in research and attracted little controversy among the group, this cannot be said of the possible IFD category. There is much confusion about the difference between a host factor and a risk factor. As before, a host factor has been defined as a characteristic of individuals clearly predisposed to, and not simply at risk of, an IFD [ 1 ]. For example, while impaired gut wall integrity through surgery or illness may increase the risk of candidiasis, it was not considered specific enough to warrant inclusion as a host factor.

span.label: AND THE UNCERTAIN CATEGORY IS THE CONTESTED ONE: `While definitions of proven and probable disease HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO BE RELIABLE IN RESEARCH and attracted LITTLE CONTROVERSY among the group, THIS CANNOT BE SAID OF THE POSSIBLE IFD CATEGORY.` `Possible` is what remains when a host factor and a clinical feature are present and the mycology is absent - **a category defined by a missing measurement**, which is why its boundary is the one nobody agrees on
span.quote: While definitions of proven and probable disease have been shown to be reliable in research and attracted little controversy among the group, this cannot be said of the possible IFD category. There is much confusion about the difference between a host factor and a risk factor. As before, a host factor has been defined as a characteristic of individuals clearly predisposed to, and not simply at risk of, an IFD [ 1 ]. For example, while impaired gut wall integrity through surgery or illness may increase the risk of candidiasis, it was not considered specific enough to warrant inclusion as a host factor.

span.label: AND THE DIAGNOSTIC TESTS CARRY THEIR OWN SCOPE LIMITS INTO THE DEFINITION: BDG is refused as evidence for a specific disease - `the group DID NOT SUPPORT the use of serum BDG TO RULE IN patients for clinical trials or for defining IA or IC, AS BDG DETECTION IS NOT SPECIFIC FOR ANY ONE IFD`; tissue histology `SIGNIFIES PROVEN FUNGAL DISEASE BUT NOT THE IDENTITY OF THE FUNGUS INVOLVED`; and T2Candida's predictive value `INCREASES FROM 62% ... TO 92%` with the population. **Each test answers a different question, and the definition has to say which**
span.quote: The group did not support the use of serum BDG to rule in patients for clinical trials or for defining IA or IC, as BDG detection is not specific for any one IFD.

span.label: AND A STANDARD WAS SET AS CRITERIA RATHER THAN AS A METHOD: `There are relatively few commercial PCR assays, and MOST INVESTIGATORS HAVE DEVELOPED METHODS IN-HOUSE. As such, the FPCRI was established TO DEVELOP CRITERIA FOR Aspergillus PCR RATHER THAN A STANDARDIZED METHOD PER SE.` **Standardising the output instead of the procedure** - the only move available when the procedures are already heterogeneous, and the reason PCR could be admitted in 2019 after exclusion in 2008
span.quote: There are relatively few commercial PCR assays, and most investigators have developed methods in-house. As such, the FPCRI was established to develop criteria for Aspergillus PCR rather than a standardized method per se.

span.label: **THE PAPER SAYS ITS OWN CATEGORIES EXCLUDE REAL DISEASE**: `We ACKNOWLEDGE THE LIMITATIONS OF THESE DEFINITIONS, INCLUDING THE EXCLUSION OF CERTAIN CASES OF IFD. However, the reliance on host factors, clinical features, and mycologic evidence to define IFD IN SELECTED POPULATIONS has proven its value for clinical trials.` A research definition is allowed to be narrower than the disease; **what it is not allowed to do is be read as a prevalence**
span.quote: In summary, these revised definitions represent consensus expert opinion based on the best available evidence. As such, they will need to be reviewed regularly for their utility and relevance and, where possible, extended to other populations affected by IFDs. We acknowledge the limitations of these definitions, including the exclusion of certain cases of IFD.

span.label: AND THE HOST-FACTOR LIST IS CONSERVATIVE BY ADMISSION, IN A CHANGING POPULATION: `We also recognize that OUR DEFINITION OF A HOST FACTOR ERRS ON THE SIDE OF CONSERVATISM GIVEN THE INCREASING USE OF DRUGS SUCH AS MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES for treating a variety of conditions.` **The denominator of at-risk patients is growing faster than the list that defines it**, and the definition will therefore miss more cases over time by construction
span.quote: We also recognize that our definition of a host factor errs on the side of conservatism given the increasing use of drugs such as monoclonal antibodies for treating a variety of conditions.

span.label: AND THE 2008 VERSION'S FAILURES ARE THE MAP OF THIS ONE'S EXPOSURE: `the definitions were UNSUITABLE FOR PATIENTS ... IN INTENSIVE CARE UNITS OR IN PEDIATRICS, DATA WERE INSUFFICIENT to establish appropriate thresholds ..., and there was UNCERTAINTY ABOUT THE ROLE of (1,3)-beta-D glucan. Furthermore, ... PCR-BASED TESTS WERE EXCLUDED BECAUSE OF LACK OF STANDARDIZATION.` Eleven years of studies used a definition its own successors call unsuitable for two whole populations
span.quote: The 2008 definitions had their shortcomings, including the facts that the definitions were unsuitable for patients with IFD in the setting of intensive care units (ICUs) or in pediatrics, data were insufficient to establish appropriate thresholds for detecting Aspergillus galactomannan (GM), and there was uncertainty about the role of (1,3)-beta-D glucan (BDG). Furthermore, nucleic acid amplification including polymerase chain reaction (PCR)–based tests were excluded because of lack of standardization and validation. Definitions for cryptococcosis and endemic mycoses also needed clarification, and there were no definitions for pneumocystosis.

span.label: AND ONE OF THE TEN WORKING GROUPS COULD NOT DO ITS JOB: `group 10 (IFD definitions in ICU patients) WAS UNABLE TO GENERATE RECOMMENDATIONS THAT PRESERVED A LEVEL OF CERTAINTY CONSISTENT WITH THE EXISTING DEFINITIONS except for proven IFD.` The ICU population named as a gap in 2008 is still outside the definitions in 2019, and the reason is that the certainty the categories require cannot be reached there
span.quote: However, group 10 (IFD definitions in ICU patients) was unable to generate recommendations that preserved a level of certainty consistent with the existing definitions except for proven IFD ( Table 1 ) and therefore undertook a separate initiative [ 8 ].

span.label: AND THE SAME SPECIES QUESTION IS ANSWERED BOTH WAYS ON ONE PAGE: `IDENTIFICATION TO THE SPECIES LEVEL for Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii HAS BECOME INCREASINGLY IMPORTANT based on reports that suggest DIFFERENT clinical presentations, outcomes, and responses to antifungal therapy` - and then `Outcomes for HIV-associated cryptococcosis due to C. neoformans and C. gattii APPEAR TO BE SIMILAR, and IDENTIFICATION TO THE SPECIES LEVEL MAY BE UNNECESSARY.` **Whether a distinction matters depends on the host**, and both halves are printed without a rule for choosing between them
span.quote: Identification to the species level for Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii has become increasingly important based on reports that suggest different clinical presentations, outcomes, and responses to antifungal therapy between these 2 species [ 71 , 72 ]. Verification of species that use CGB (L-canavanine, glycine, bromthymol blue) agar or matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization–time of flight mass spectrometry is recommended. Outcomes for HIV-associated cryptococcosis due to C. neoformans and C. gattii appear to be similar, and identification to the species level may be unnecessary [ 73 , 74 ].

span.label: AND THE DISCLOSURES ARE EXTENSIVE AND UNIFORM ACROSS 62 AUTHORS: `J. P. DONNELLY REPORTS PERSONAL FEES FROM F2G LTD, GILEAD SCIENCES, AND PFIZER outside the submitted work.` Comparable statements follow for most of the author list, naming the manufacturers of antifungals and of the diagnostic assays whose thresholds this document sets. All declared, none hidden - **and the panel that fixes an assay's cutoff is advised by people paid by the companies selling the assays**, which is a fact about how this field is organised
span.quote: J. P. Donnelly reports personal fees from F2G Ltd, Gilead Sciences, and Pfizer outside the submitted work.

span.label: refusing BDG as evidence for any specific fungal disease, while accepting it for probable IFD in general
span.note: eliminates: a non-specific biomarker being used to rule patients into a trial of one particular infection · outcome: held
span.quote: The group did not support the use of serum BDG to rule in patients for clinical trials or for defining IA or IC, as BDG detection is not specific for any one IFD.

span.label: defining a host factor as predisposition rather than raised risk, and testing the rule on impaired gut wall integrity
span.note: eliminates: a category that would absorb most intensive-care patients · outcome: held
span.quote: While definitions of proven and probable disease have been shown to be reliable in research and attracted little controversy among the group, this cannot be said of the possible IFD category. There is much confusion about the difference between a host factor and a risk factor. As before, a host factor has been defined as a characteristic of individuals clearly predisposed to, and not simply at risk of, an IFD [ 1 ]. For example, while impaired gut wall integrity through surgery or illness may increase the risk of candidiasis, it was not considered specific enough to warrant inclusion as a host factor.

span.label: requiring DNA sequencing after PCR, and only in laboratories with a proven record, before tissue findings identify a fungus
span.note: eliminates: an identification from histology alone, which `signifies proven fungal disease but not the identity of the fungus involved` · outcome: held
span.quote: Tissue diagnosis requires the presence of fungal elements in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue and signifies proven fungal disease but not the identity of the fungus involved.

span.label: a host factor
span.quote: While definitions of proven and probable disease have been shown to be reliable in research and attracted little controversy among the group, this cannot be said of the possible IFD category. There is much confusion about the difference between a host factor and a risk factor. As before, a host factor has been defined as a characteristic of individuals clearly predisposed to, and not simply at risk of, an IFD [ 1 ]. For example, while impaired gut wall integrity through surgery or illness may increase the risk of candidiasis, it was not considered specific enough to warrant inclusion as a host factor.

span.label: definitions of IFD required for clinical research
span.term: definitions of IFD required for clinical research
span.quote: Throughout this process, we have emphasized the need to differentiate between definitions of IFD required for clinical research from those that influence clinical practice. In clinical practice, many would administer an antifungal agent to any patient at risk of IFD when fungi are detected by biomarkers in serum, plasma, whole blood, or relevant body site fluid without there being sufficient evidence to satisfy the consensus definitions of IFD.

span.label: those that influence clinical practice
span.quote: Throughout this process, we have emphasized the need to differentiate between definitions of IFD required for clinical research from those that influence clinical practice. In clinical practice, many would administer an antifungal agent to any patient at risk of IFD when fungi are detected by biomarkers in serum, plasma, whole blood, or relevant body site fluid without there being sufficient evidence to satisfy the consensus definitions of IFD.

span.label: Exposure to 1 of these fungi
span.quote: Exposure to 1 of these fungi is defined as a history of residence in an endemic area, no matter how remote, travel to an endemic area, or contact with fomites such as soil or vegetation that is derived from an endemic area.

span.label: a history of residence in an endemic area
span.term: a history of residence in an endemic area
span.quote: Exposure to 1 of these fungi is defined as a history of residence in an endemic area, no matter how remote, travel to an endemic area, or contact with fomites such as soil or vegetation that is derived from an endemic area.

span.label: Cryptococcus neoformans
span.quote: Identification to the species level for Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii has become increasingly important based on reports that suggest different clinical presentations, outcomes, and responses to antifungal therapy between these 2 species [ 71 , 72 ]. Verification of species that use CGB (L-canavanine, glycine, bromthymol blue) agar or matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization–time of flight mass spectrometry is recommended. Outcomes for HIV-associated cryptococcosis due to C. neoformans and C. gattii appear to be similar, and identification to the species level may be unnecessary [ 73 , 74 ].

span.label: Cryptococcus gattii
span.quote: Identification to the species level for Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii has become increasingly important based on reports that suggest different clinical presentations, outcomes, and responses to antifungal therapy between these 2 species [ 71 , 72 ]. Verification of species that use CGB (L-canavanine, glycine, bromthymol blue) agar or matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization–time of flight mass spectrometry is recommended. span.label: Exposure to mold-active antifungals
span.quote: Exposure to mold-active antifungals compromises the utility of the GM test for IA [ 38 ] by reducing its sensitivity [ 39 ]. Therefore, caution should be exercised when GM is found to be absent from serum or plasma in patients receiving mold-active antifungals.

span.label: the utility of the GM test

span.quote: Exposure to mold-active antifungals compromises the utility of the GM test for IA [ 38 ] by reducing its sensitivity [ 39 ]. Therefore, caution should be exercised when GM is found to be absent from serum or plasma in patients receiving mold-active antifungals.

span.label: `proven` IFD - histology, culture or a sterile-site specimen. `Can apply to ANY patient, regardless of whether the patient is immunocompromised` - the only one of the three categories that is not restricted by host
span.quote: The category of proven IFD can apply to any patient, regardless of whether the patient is immunocompromised. The probable and possible categories are proposed for immunocompromised patients only, except for endemic mycoses.

span.label: `probable` IFD - a host factor AND a clinical feature AND mycological evidence, `proposed for immunocompromised patients only, except for endemic mycoses`. **Expanded in this revision without changing the word**
span.quote: There is no change in the classifications of “proven,” “probable,” and “possible” IFD, although the definition of “probable” has been expanded and the scope of the category “possible” has been diminished.

span.label: `possible` IFD - a host factor and a clinical feature with the mycology missing. The category that `attracted controversy` where the other two did not - **defined by an absent measurement**
span.quote: While definitions of proven and probable disease have been shown to be reliable in research and attracted little controversy among the group, this cannot be said of the possible IFD category. There is much confusion about the difference between a host factor and a risk factor. As before, a host factor has been defined as a characteristic of individuals clearly predisposed to, and not simply at risk of, an IFD [ 1 ]. For example, while impaired gut wall integrity through surgery or illness may increase the risk of candidiasis, it was not considered specific enough to warrant inclusion as a host factor.

span.label: `host factor` - `a characteristic of individuals CLEARLY PREDISPOSED TO, AND NOT SIMPLY AT RISK OF, an IFD`. Impaired gut wall integrity raises the risk of candidiasis and is refused as a host factor for not being specific enough

span.quote: The 2008 definitions had their shortcomings, including the facts that the definitions were unsuitable for patients with IFD in the setting of intensive care units (ICUs) or in pediatrics, data were insufficient to establish appropriate thresholds for detecting Aspergillus galactomannan (GM), and there was uncertainty about the role of (1,3)-beta-D glucan (BDG). Furthermore, nucleic acid amplification including polymerase chain reaction (PCR)–based tests were excluded because of lack of standardization and validation. Definitions for cryptococcosis and endemic mycoses also needed clarification, and there were no definitions for pneumocystosis.
